sanctuary_sites: CNS (high relapse risk; CNS prophylaxis often considered in selected high-risk patients, but is not uniformly strongly recommended for all cases)

biomarkers.name: MYC rearrangement + BCL2 rearrangement (double-hit) or all three including BCL6 (triple-hit)
biomarkers.clinical_use: WHO 2022 requires MYC + BCL2 rearrangement for the high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements diagnosis; cases may also have concurrent BCL6 rearrangement (triple-hit). MYC + BCL6 without BCL2 is no longer included in this entity and is generally classified as DLBCL, NOS or HGBL, NOS depending on morphology. Intensified regimens such as DA-EPOCH-R are often preferred in practice. Outcomes after CAR-T have been reported, but poor response is not established as a defining feature.

biomarkers.name: CD20, CD19, CD22, CD79b (same treatment biomarkers as DLBCL)
biomarkers.prevalence: Frequent expression of pan-B-cell markers, though not universal in every case

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Diffuse infiltrate of medium to large B lymphocytes with intermediate morphology between DLBCL and Burkitt lymphoma; starry-sky pattern in some cases
variants: HGBL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (DHL)
HGBL with MYC and BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements (THL)

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Aggressive with high proliferative index; TP53 co-alteration common; extranodal involvement especially CNS/BM
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Diffuse effacement with starry-sky pattern (macrophages engulfing apoptotic cells)

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Germinal centre B cells with concurrent MYC and BCL2 rearrangements driving intermediate phenotype between DLBCL and Burkitt lymphoma
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Intermediate morphology between DLBCL and Burkitt lymphoma; starry-sky pattern in some cases; retains B-cell markers with germinal centre programme (BCL6+, CD10+, BCL2+)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Concurrent MYC + BCL2 (or MYC + BCL2 + BCL6) rearrangements represent lineage-relevant events combining MYC deregulation with BCL2-mediated anti-apoptotic signaling; TP53 mutations are frequent co-alterations
